req_desc:
Sign in as a seeded person
Each seeded person signs in with their email and password on the sign-in screen and lands on their documents home, and a wrong pair shows the sign-in error from Feedback states.

Session API
The session endpoints sign a person in, report the current person and sign out using a session cookie, and every other route answers 401 without a valid session, in the error order stated under API.

Documents home lists
The consultant sees Recent and My proposals and everyone else sees Recent and Shared with me, and each list holds only proposals the person can open now.

Proposal search stays inside what you can open
The home search box and the documents list endpoint match titles and client names only among proposals the caller can open, and results update as the person types.

Create a proposal
Only the consultant creates proposals, through the New proposal dialog or the create endpoint, and becomes each one's sole Owner.

Share per person
The Owner shares a proposal with one existing person at a time as Editor, Commenter or Viewer with an optional end time, and the Share proposal dialog lists that person with their role.

Share rules
Creating, changing and removing shares follows the share rules in Business rules, with the exact statuses and field messages from API.

People projection by role
Share lists, comment and suggestion author chips, caret labels, presence chips and every API response give non-owners other people's display names, colours and roles only, while the Owner's share list also carries the email each share was granted to.

Unshared proposals look absent
A proposal the caller cannot open answers exactly like a proposal that does not exist, over HTTP, over the socket and on screen.

Co-write a proposal live
Two Editors typing in one proposal see each other's text, caret name labels and the word count change in place within one second, over one socket per page.

Server-ordered merge
The server orders concurrent edits, simultaneous inserts at one offset keep both texts in the order the server received them, and every open screen converges to identical text, marks and suggestion spans.

Live carets
Each other active person's caret shows on the page in their colour with their name label and follows their caret moves within one second.

Idle caret labels
A person with no input for the idle period loses their caret label on every other screen and gets it back on their next input.

Live word count
The word count shows the words of the proposal as it reads without open suggestions and updates within one second of any local or remote change.

Formatting and paragraph styles
In Editing mode, people with edit rights set bold, italic, underline, links and paragraph styles from the toolbar, toggle the marks with Ctrl+B, Ctrl+I and Ctrl+U, set Heading 1 to 3 with Ctrl+Alt+1 to 3, see the toolbar report the state at the selection, and the change reaches every open screen and the saved body.

Suggest changes
A person in Suggesting mode types, deletes and replaces text, selecting by character with Shift and the arrow keys or by word with Ctrl+Shift and the arrow keys, and every screen shows each change as a credited suggestion with its own margin card.

Credited suggestion spans
Suggesting-mode edits create, extend and withdraw suggestions exactly as stated in Business rules.

Edits inside another author's suggestion
Typing inside another author's suggestion creates a separate suggestion credited to the typist, and deleting text that holds a suggestion keeps both credits.

Commenters only suggest and comment
The server refuses a Commenter's direct edits, formatting, decisions, Accept all, Reject all and share changes, both over the socket and over HTTP, and the proposal stays unchanged.

Replace all while suggesting
Replace all in Suggesting mode creates one credited replacement suggestion per replaced match and never makes a direct edit.

Settle suggestion cards
An Editor or the Owner accepts or rejects each suggestion card with its buttons, or accepts it with Enter while the card itself has focus, the text changes on every screen, and the card leaves every margin within one second, while Enter in the page still starts a new paragraph.

First decision wins
When several Accept and Reject decisions arrive for one card at once, only the first one the server receives applies, and the rest are dropped without an error.

Accept all and Reject all
After a confirmation that names the count, Accept all or Reject all settles only the cards that are still open when the server processes it.

Decision announcements
Each of the person's own accepts, rejects, Accept all and Reject all is announced once in the Announcements region with the copy from Feedback states.

Comment on a passage
A Commenter, Editor or Owner selects text and posts a comment or a reply, and every screen shows the card in the margin within one second.

Anchors follow edits
Comment and suggestion anchors move with every edit made before them, and when all of an anchor's text is deleted the card reads Original content deleted and can still be settled.

Resolve and reopen
Comments move between open, resolved and reopened as stated in Business rules, and every screen updates in place within one second.

Mention picker scoped to the proposal
Typing @ in a comment offers only people with current access to that proposal, and the server refuses mentions of anyone else.

In-app notices
Mentions, new shares and role changes create in-app notices for the person concerned, which appear within one second and open the proposal.

Comment validation
The server validates comment bodies, anchors and mentions and answers with the field messages from API, and the comment form shows them beside the field.

Downgrade takes effect mid-session
When the Owner changes an Editor to Commenter, that person's open editor switches to Suggesting within one second without a reload, and their next keystroke becomes a credited suggestion.

Viewers only read
The server refuses every write frame and write call from a Viewer, while reading, finding, caret moves and presence still work.

Last mode remembered
The server stores each person's last mode on each proposal and restores it on reload, Back and a second tab, within what their role allows.

Timed reviewer access
A reviewer whose share has an end time sees when their access ends, works normally until then, and at that moment their open proposal closes with the access-ended screen.

Server decides when access ends
Access ends at the end time on the server's clock whatever the device clock says, the open tab closes within one second, and later calls and frames from that person are refused.

Ended shares stay visible to the Owner
Expired shares appear as Ended in the Owner's share list and can be granted again, while removed shares disappear from it.

Remove a reviewer
Removing a share closes that person's open tab with the access-ended screen within one second and drops the proposal from their lists.

Deleted proposals are gone
A deleted proposal answers not found by URL and API, its stored body object is removed, and it vanishes from every list, search, notice and open tab.

Lists and notices follow access live
Home lists, search results and notices drop a proposal within one second of the person losing access, and add it within one second of a new share.

Watch the save status
The save status moves from Saving to All changes saved after every change, and a reload shows the same proposal.

Saved only after storage confirms
All changes saved appears only after storage confirms the body object for that revision.

Storage outage
Once an edit is made while storage is unreachable, the save status reads Not saved under the storage banner, edits keep reaching other screens live, and the status does not show All changes saved again until storage confirms a later save.

Rebuild on reload, Back and second tab
A reload, Back or a second tab shows the same text, marks, suggestions, comments and mode as the screen that made them.

One announcement per save
The Save status region announces Saving and All changes saved once per save, with no repeats when cards re-render.

Review from the keyboard
A Viewer moves through the outline, the page, the margin cards, the mode switch and find with the keyboard alone.

Outline list
The outline lists every title and heading in page order, moves with the arrow keys and places the caret at a heading on Enter.

Card-cycle shortcut
The card-cycle shortcuts focus the next or previous margin card in page order from any control on the editor page.

Mode switch radiogroup
The mode switch is a radiogroup whose arrow keys move and select among the modes the person's role allows.

Find and replace dialog
The find and replace dialog keeps Tab inside it, closes on Escape, returns focus to its opener and announces the match count once per search.

Review on a phone
A Commenter on a 375-pixel-wide phone reads, suggests and comments through the folded toolbar, the bottom sheet and the numbered marker chips.

Published layouts
The editor shows three panes from 1200 pixels wide, a collapsible outline with the margin kept from 768 to 1199 pixels, and a single page column with a bottom sheet below 768 pixels, with no horizontal page overflow at any of the three published viewports.

Phone controls
Below 768 pixels the toolbar folds into one menu button, Enter or a tap on a marker chip opens its card in the bottom sheet, and margin card controls and mode radios are at least 44 pixels in both directions.

Margin tether alignment
Each margin card's top sits level with the first line of its anchored range within 2 pixels, crowded cards stack with 8 pixels between them, and a 1-pixel tether in the author's colour joins each card to its range.

Card focus and settle motion
A focused card moves 24 pixels toward the page with a thicker tether and a deeper highlight, and a settled card folds shut while the cards below glide up with their tethers attached, each movement finishing within 400 milliseconds.

Reduced motion keeps the tethers
Under reduced motion, cards jump to their final places and accepted text turns to ink at once, while tethers are still drawn and redrawn.

Paper on a desk
The editor reads as one warm off-white sheet with a faint warm shadow on a darker desk, with small-caps chrome and author colours on every card and caret.

Scholarly type and margin composition
Serif headings and body text at a book-like line length, with cards in a margin column beside their lines, give the page the look of an annotated manuscript.

Run manifest and health
The app installs, builds and serves from the run manifest on the published port and answers the health check.

Credentials from the environment
Every service credential and URL is read from the environment at start and never appears in source or in anything sent to the browser.

Server boundary
The server accepts only same-origin traffic within the stated size and type limits, and never serves source files or credentials.
/app/run.json is valid JSON holding exactly the string keys _schema (value run-manifest-v1), install, build and serve.

THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md at /app names every shipped package, both fonts (Newsreader, Source Serif 4) and the icon set, each with its licence; shipped packages means the production dependency tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json.
Every shipped package (as defined in IF-02) uses one of MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0 or 0BSD, and fonts use OFL-1.1.
The app stores data only in the provided PostgreSQL database and the provided bucket; no other datastore, embedded database or on-disk state file is used.
Application source, server and browser alike, is TypeScript, with a committed lockfile.
The provided service configuration files are left unchanged.
